key_insight: Reintroducing and institutionalizing 'Reusability Reports' and clear code-reporting practices can counteract the loss of reproducibility and reusability caused by the rapid pace of AI/ML publication driven by large language models.
problem_solved: The paper tackles declining reproducibility and poor code-sharing/reporting practices that accompany 'fast science'—high publication velocity and fragmented artifact availability—making validation and reuse difficult.
method: Propose renewed use of Reusability Reports as a standard article/appendix format to highlight code, environment, and evaluation details.
Offer a concise checklist/framework for reporting artifacts (code, dependencies, data access, evaluation scripts, and expected outputs).
Recommend community-level interventions: journal policies, incentives, and tooling to standardize and automate reproducibility checks.
impact: Adopting these practices helps practitioners verify results, reliably reuse models and code, and reduce duplicated effort—improving the pace and trustworthiness of AI research.
visual_elements: One-page Reusability Report template showing required artifact sections (code, env, data, metrics).
Checklist infographic that highlights must-share items (repo, run commands, seed, eval scripts).
Before/after timeline illustrating rapid publication vs. reproducibility outcomes with/without reports.
Icons representing policy, tooling, and community incentives to show systemic levers.
paper_title: Recognizing reproducibility and reusability in times of fast science
